title: Book One · Chapter 14: Mum's Scissors
story:
Ronan finds Mum's scissors beside a folded blue shirt.

They are much bigger than the school scissors. The handles shine. He puts two fingers through one handle and lifts them.

"Put those down, please," Mum says.

"I need a tail."

"You have a whole back of your own."

"For the kite."

"Those are for cloth. Please ask me first. Then you can take them."

Ronan puts the scissors on the table. He is careful not to let the points hang over the edge.

"May I borrow them?"

"No."

He waits. He said please. Mum still said no. He looks at the scissors again.

Mum sees him waiting.

"Paper makes these less sharp. I need them for work."

"What work?"

She holds up the blue shirt. The side has opened. A little bundle of other clothes is beside her bag.

"Mrs Lan asked about this. Another neighbour has two pairs of trousers. I will try one pair first. Then I will check the time."

"Will you get paid?"

"Yes, I will get a little money. First I need to do the work properly."

Ronan looks at the cloth under her elbow. It is blue, the right colour for a kite tail.

"Can I have that bit?"

"That bit is someone's sleeve."

"What bit can I have?"

Mum takes a bag from under the bed. There are small pieces of cloth inside. She spreads them out. Some are wide. Some are no bigger than Ronan's hand.

"These are mine. You may choose from these."

Ronan finds three blue strips and a yellow square. The strips are not the same blue. One is almost white.

"They don't match."

"Do the colours need to match?" Mum asks.

He thinks of the brown kite. He lays the blue pieces in a row. One is dark. One is pale. He likes the colours together.

"I'll ask Leo."

He leaves the cloth on his bed and goes to wash his hands. The yard tap works with one smooth turn. Ronan closes it carefully. He watches for one drop. None comes.

Leo arrives. Mum is sewing by the window. They show her their tail plan. She gives them the little scissors and helps with the thickest strip. The boys cut the other pieces on a board.

Leo ties a very large knot. Half the strip is inside the knot.

"It looks like a blue onion," Ronan says.

"You tie one."

Ronan ties one. He lifts the cloth. His knot comes undone. They try smaller knots and pull them gently to check.

Mum keeps sewing. The boys show her their knots. Sometimes she looks. Sometimes she says she needs to finish her stitch first.

Before dinner, Ronan returns the scissors. He also gives her a blue thread he finds on the floor.

"Thank you," she says. "The scissors matter more than that thread."

"I brought both."

She takes both with a very serious face.

The new tail lies beside the kite. It has three blues, one yellow square, and several tight knots. Ronan touches a loose end. Mum's blue shirt is nearly whole again. His kite is getting a little longer. Mum puts her good scissors away. Ronan brings back the little ones. He puts them beside her sewing box. The good cloth and his tail are separate again.
studyGuide:
---

重点表达：borrow＝借用；sharp＝锋利的；knots＝绳结；returns＝归还。

辅助理解：stitch＝针脚；thread＝线；comes undone＝松开、散开。

理解问题：

1. Ronan 为什么拿不到 Mum 的大剪刀？
2. 他怎样在不使用好布料的情况下做出尾巴？
